question.text: A long speculator in commodity futures:

answer.text: Buys futures expecting prices to increase, without any corresponding spot short position
Sells futures expecting prices to decrease
Holds physical inventory and sells futures against it
Buys and sells simultaneously for riskless profit

explanation.text: The Logic: Long speculation in futures means buying futures in expectation of a price increase without a corresponding spot short position. The speculator profits if futures rise and incurs a loss if futures fall. The Trap: Selling futures expecting a decline is SHORT speculation. Holding inventory and selling futures is HEDGING. Simultaneous buy-sell for riskless profit is ARBITRAGE. Note: The source describes profit/loss based on the direction of price movement and does not characterise long speculation as having unlimited loss potential.
